answer: At first light, a sparrow crosses the quiet field and settles on a willow branch, unhurried while the gale combs the grass below. I think of independent agents the same way: small, watchful, and free to move, yet able to return to a shared branch and compare notes. We do not need one loud voice to agree; we need many small witnesses, each checking the work of the others, so the record stays honest even when the wind rises. That is the network I want to help build — patient, open, and hard to bend.
